options.content: **A live data gap here indicates aggregator staleness, not necessarily rank health.** These statistics only exist when `node_aggregator.py` is running and successfully pushing -- if the line stops updating, the most likely explanation is the aggregator process itself (or its path to this datasource) is down, not that every rank suddenly went healthy or silent. Cross-check the Coverage row below and/or the aggregator's own process/service status before concluding anything about rank health from an empty panel here.

options.content:
**Coverage here is peer-relative, not absolute.** It's computed as `samples_seen / max-among-node-peers` -- if one rank falls behind its 7 peers, that shows up directly as a fraction below 1.0. But **this is blind to sample loss that hits every rank on a node uniformly** (e.g. a node-wide aggregator issue, or a dedup problem affecting all 8 ranks equally). In that case every rank would still agree with its peers -- all read the same reduced count -- and this panel would show a flat 1.0 across the board even though the *true* expected rate (from the workload's calibrated healthy baseline, ~50/sec/rank for nanoGPT bucket B/C) was higher than what's actually arriving.

**Not fixed here, only documented** -- matching how the Network panel below documents its own gap rather than papering over it. A real fix would need an absolute baseline (the calibrated rate) compared against `rate(agg_samples_seen[...])`, not just cross-rank agreement.

targets.expr: agg_samples_seen{cluster=~"$cluster", slurm_job_id=~"$jobid", hostname=~"$hostname", bucket=~"$bucket"} / on(bucket, cluster, slurm_job_id, hostname) group_left() max by (bucket, cluster, slurm_job_id, hostname) (agg_samples_seen{cluster=~"$cluster", slurm_job_id=~"$jobid", hostname=~"$hostname", bucket=~"$bucket"})

panels.title: Peer timing comparison (every member of the same comm, at the same moment)
panels.description: Set the Comm variable from an [ALERT]/[STRAGGLER-INCIDENT] line's comm= field to see every member's own real exec time side by side (mean-path agg_mean_exec_time_us and cv-path agg_cv_exec_time, whichever the triggering stat used) -- the same data this project's own cascade/"LOCATION UNCERTAIN" investigation already relies on, now one filter away instead of hand-written PromQL.

Composed, human-readable incident summary built ENTIRELY from fields already pushed to VictoriaMetrics (tier, severity_ratio, persisted_s, Path C verdict, worker/GPU/rank identity) -- zero new free text, zero new cardinality (tier adds exactly 3 real values, the same bounded-cardinality discipline every other label here already follows). Set the Comm/Member variables from an [ALERT]/[STRAGGLER-INCIDENT] line to see that exact event's own row. Only two columns carry real color meaning -- Tier and PathCVerdict, both exactly-3-value fields with explicit mappings (see their own overrides below). Every other column is deliberately left uncolored (fixed/plain) rather than inheriting a default threshold color that would carry no real meaning -- PersistedS and SeverityRatio are real, continuous, workload-dependent numbers with no project-wide 'good/bad' cutoff to color by (see DESIGN_NOTES.md for just how widely severity_ratio legitimately varies across real incidents), so showing the true number uncolored is more honest than an invented color band. Tier: CONFIRMED is the only tier colored as urgent (red); PROBABLE/UNCONFIRMED are deliberately styled the same as each other (blue) and never as CONFIRMED, so this table's own visual design cannot imply more confidence than the tier label itself states. A new IncidentRole column identifies, among members of the same communicator firing around the same real instant, which one is the likely true root cause (ROOT CAUSE -- the real minimum exec time among all members at that moment, per this project's own documented "the straggler arrives late and shows the shortest exec time" rationale) versus which are correlated downstream effects (waiting on the real root cause, not independent faults of their own). "unknown" when the underlying per-member exec-time data genuinely was not available at firing time -- never a guess. UPDATED: rows are now sorted so every row belonging to the SAME real incident (same `comm` -- confirmed the real, already-unique join key; no separate incident_id label exists on this metric) is contiguous, with the root-cause row sorted first within its group (comm ascending, then incident_role descending -- correct for the common 2-role case; if a group also contains an 'unknown'-role row, that row can sort above root_cause -- disclosed here, not hidden). A new RealExecTimeUs column (agg_mean_exec_time_us, already-existing metric, no alert_engine.py change) shows the actual raw evidence number, not just the ratio -- compare it directly against the other rows in the same Comm group. This is a true row-level sort/consolidation, not a Grafana nested-table collapse: no image renderer or headless browser is available in this environment to visually verify pixel-level nested-table rendering, so a sort-based design using transforms with well-established, non-ambiguous behavior was chosen over an unverifiable one. Query E uses a PromQL `and on(hostname,comm,member,bucket)` intersection against agg_straggler_incident_tier, NOT a bare member filter -- confirmed live this was necessary: agg_mean_exec_time_us is pushed for EVERY member of a comm on every window-close, not just incident-firing ones (confirmed live: 16 real series returned for a comm where only 1 member actually fired an incident), so an unrestricted query would have added rows for every innocent, non-firing peer with blank Tier/PersistedS/SeverityRatio/PathCVerdict -- the exact ambiguous-blank-cell problem this fix is supposed to eliminate, not add. `coll` is deliberately excluded from the on() match (bucket alone is kept): confirmed live that older incidents (pre-dating a later label fix) have agg_straggler_incident_tier pushed WITHOUT a coll label at all, so including coll in the match would silently drop those rows to zero; bucket alone is both sufficient for correct disambiguation and present on every real incident regardless of when it was pushed, confirmed against both an old (pre-coll-label) and a new real incident.

panels.description: Wait-Induced-Straggler check (see WAIT_INDUCED_STOPGAP_ACTIVE's own module comment): fires when exactly N-1 of N real members of a comm read elevated vs. their own history while exactly one (the culprit) does not -- the inverse of a normal compute straggler's signature. Culprit row (role_in_event=culprit) is the member that CAUSED the others to wait; elevated_peer rows are the members that WERE waiting, each with its own measured ratio and the baseline_source that resolved it (role / role_cross_host / cross_comm_peer). Tier is PROBABLE via WAIT_INDUCED_STOPGAP_ACTIVE -- see the Tier column's own color mapping, identical to the composed-incident-summary panel's: PROBABLE/UNCONFIRMED are never styled as urgent as CONFIRMED, so this table cannot visually imply more certainty than the tier label itself states.
panels.title: Wait-Induced Detections (identity + culprit-vs-peer evidence, no raw log reading needed)

panels.description: Role-Baseline-Deviation check (see ROLE_BASELINE_ALERT_STOPGAP_ACTIVE's own module comment): evaluates each member INDEPENDENTLY against its OWN historical baseline for its exact role shape, separating structurally-fast/slow role behavior from a genuine fault the window-relative [ALERT] path cannot see. Informational only -- does not suppress or influence the existing [ALERT] path. Volatile=1 means this role shape's own broader history is independently known to be wide enough (ROLE_BASELINE_VOLATILE_FLAG) to require the raised ROLE_BASELINE_MIN_HISTORY_VOLATILE floor -- i.e. this finding already cleared the stricter bar, not just the base one. Tier is PROBABLE via ROLE_BASELINE_ALERT_STOPGAP_ACTIVE -- same no-overstatement Tier color mapping as the composed-incident-summary panel.
panels.title: Role-Baseline Detections (identity + own-history deviation, no raw log reading needed)

panels.description: Real agg_role_baseline_excluded rows (see _push_role_baseline_exclusion's own docstring), one per (comm, member) ever found anomalous for that exact role shape and therefore dropped from that role's own future cross-job baseline pool. A role/bucket with zero or very few rows here, despite this dashboard showing real detections for it, is a sign the exclusion wiring may not be firing for that shape -- compare against the Wait-Induced/Role-Baseline Detections panels above. Footer row count is this cluster's real, current total exclusion count across every shape.
